title: Two permutation pruning rules restricting indices and values
summary: Compare side by side the two pruning conditions: no repeated indices along a path (selected) and no repeated values within a round (duplicated).
context: The input array is choices = [1, 1, 2] at indices 0, 1, and 2. Below, "first 1" and "second 1" distinguish indices 0 and 1; the figure places a hat over the second 1 as an identity marker, though both have numeric value 1.
description: Black scissors mark path-index pruning, which forbids reusing an index already on the current path until backtracking makes that index available again. Red scissors mark same-round value pruning: duplicated records only values not skipped by the black scissors and actually chosen during the current call's round, and each recursive call creates a fresh set whose scope differs from selected.

Each square node here represents a single choice, the prefix in the table concatenates the choices along the path from the root to that node, and a complete root-to-leaf path forms a permutation. The first table below separates the black and red scissors shown in the figure into two columns; a cell listing multiple candidates corresponds to multiple pruned branches. The second 1 under the root [] and under prefix [2] is pruned by red scissors, while all branches with already used indices are pruned by black scissors. The second table lists the three unique permutations in order.

frames.title: Two permutation pruning rules restricting indices and values
frames.explanation: A single path may still pick both 1s at their two different indices in sequence; within any single round, only one branch is expanded for value 1.
